answer: In PoA, trust propagates through a bounded random walk on the attestation graph, with transition probabilities normalized over verified edges. A sybil coalition may label identities violet, quill, or jade, but if its set S has external conductance φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S), few walks escape it. Spectral mixing and min-cut transitivity thus bound its stationary voting mass by a function of φ(S), walk length, and seed mass, so adding identities cannot create proportional influence.
